decision.explanation: The governing document (General_Conditions.pdf) states that 'any delay automatically extends contract time for the length of the delay without further demonstration or timely supporting notice.' The current automatic-extension language removes all contractor obligations and should not be allowed to stand without deliberate, documented approval.

decision.recommended_action: Human review required. decision.applicability_reason: Project metadata indicates subcontractors will be used, so DelDOT 108.1 subletting limits apply.
decision.explanation: The package clause at General_Conditions.pdf|p1|L21–L22 materially deviates from the reference in two independent ways. First, it permits up to 80% of the work to be subcontracted, which means the prime need only self-perform 20% — directly conflicting with the reference requirement that the prime perform no less than 50% of the total original contract price with its own organization. Second, it states 'the prime is not responsible for subcontractor performance,' which directly negates the reference requirement that subletting does not relieve the prime of contract responsibility. No Addendum revises this provision; the governing document remains General_Conditions.pdf. Both deviations are affirmative conflicts proven by the quoted package language, not mere omissions or vague placeholders.
decision.recommended_action: Human review required. The subletting clause must be corrected to (1) require the prime to self-perform no less than 50% of the total original contract price with its own organization, and (2) confirm that subletting does not relieve the prime of contract responsibility. Both elements are materially weakened in the current package text.

decision.applicability_reason: Project metadata records an unresolved contract-change/claim scenario.
decision.explanation: The package clause deviates from the Challenge Reference Rule in two material respects. First, it states the notice window is 'sixty (60) days,' whereas the reference requires a written claim within 30 calendar days after completion of the work described in the notice of intent — a direct numerical conflict (60 days vs. 30 days). Second, the clause expressly states that 'detailed contemporaneous documentation is optional,' which directly negates the reference requirement that the notice/documentation process and supporting documents are mandatory prerequisites to a valid claim. These are affirmative conflicts with the reference, not mere paraphrases or omissions. No Addendum revises this provision, so the General_Conditions.pdf text governs and the deviations stand.
decision.recommended_action: Human review required. The claims procedure clause in General_Conditions.pdf conflicts with the reference on two points: (1) the notice/claim deadline is stated as 60 days rather than the required 30 calendar days after completion of the noticed work, and (2) contemporaneous documentation is characterized as optional rather than mandatory. Both deviations should be corrected before contract execution.

decision.applicability_reason: Project metadata records a delay/time-extension scenario.
decision.explanation: The governing clause in General_Conditions.pdf (the highest-precedence document for this provision, with no Addendum revision) states that extensions 'require the reference conditions, timely support, and demonstrated effect on contract time' and are 'not automatic for every delay.' This language incorporates by reference all three elements mandated by the Challenge Reference Rule: (1) excusable-delay/reference conditions, (2) timely written notice/support, and (3) critical-path/substantial-completion effect. The clause also expressly negates automaticity. Although the clause does not repeat the specific procedural details of DelDOT 108.7, it defers to 'the reference conditions' rather than contradicting them, which is compliant under the incorporation-by-reference principle. No affirmative conflict with the reference rule is present.
decision.recommended_action: No action required on this provision. Human reviewer may confirm that 'the reference conditions' is understood by project staff to mean DelDOT 108.7 in full, but no material deviation is identified.

criteria.challenge_reference_rule: When a delay scenario applies, an extension requires an excusable delay, a timely written request/notice under the reference process, and an effect on the critical path/substantial-completion time. Delay does not create an automatic time extension.
criteria.review_expectation: Verify time-extension language retains timely notice and excusable-delay/critical-path requirements.

decision.applicability_reason: Package includes a liquidated-damages provision or governing schedule.

This directly conflicts with the Challenge Reference Rule, which requires the LD rate to be tied to the applicable reference schedule based on contract value and time basis. The phrase 'regardless of contract value or governing schedule' is the precise language the Challenge Reference Rule identifies as a material deviation — a universal invented flat daily rate.
decision.recommended_action: Human review required. The liquidated-damages clause should be revised to tie the daily rate to the applicable DelDOT Section 108.9 schedule based on contract value, rather than imposing a flat $10,000 per day regardless of contract value or governing schedule.
